title: Thread a 273 mm CryoSleeve onto a vial-loaded aluminum CryoCane up to its top tab before transfer-racking
instruction: Slide the ivory cryo-sleeve from the prep mat onto the aluminum cryo-cane up to its bent top tab without spilling either vial, lay the sleeved cane flat inside the stainless transfer tray, and let go.
context: The hard parts: the aluminum cane starts trough-up with its 26 mm bent top tab facing the sleeve, so one hand must lift and yaw the 290 mm cane 180 degrees horizontally while keeping its open shelves level (rolling past 60 degrees or tipping steeply spills the two loose 12.5 mm vials onto the bench), while the sleeve fits only over the straight bottom foot and must be threaded coaxially over 265 mm with two hands in mid-air against sliding friction without cocking and wedging. Technicians in biological, cell-culture, IVF and biobank research labs routinely stage 1.8 mL Nunc CryoTube vials (Thermo Scientific 377267, 12.5 mm OD, sitting loose in 13.5 mm-vial troughs) on 5-place stepped aluminum Nalgene CryoCanes (5015-0001) and enclose each cane in a 273 mm PVC Nalgene CryoSleeve (5016-0001) before carrying canes in a transfer tray to vapor-phase racks, so loose tubes do not spill during handling.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left; fixed layout (nothing varies by seed). A dark blue silicone bench strip 13.0 x 60.0 x 0.2 cm (cut from a Heathrow Scientific 35 x 60 x 0.2 cm FDA food-grade silicone lab mat) is taped flat on the bench centred at (21.0, 0.0), spanning x = 14.5..27.5 and y = -30.0..+30.0, with four white alignment ticks marking the cane and sleeve ends. Behind it at (36.5, +3.5), within 3 mm and 2 degrees of bench tape marks, sits a generic open 18/10 stainless steel lab transfer tray 35.0 x 15.0 x 3.5 cm (any open tray at least 32 x 14 cm; long axis along y = -14.0..+21.0, 420 g). On the prep mat along x = 21.0: (1) a 5-place stepped aluminum Thermo Scientific Nalgene CryoCane (Cat. No. 5015-0001, 29.0 cm long, blue label on its 90-degree upturned top handling tab) lying trough-up from y = +27.8 (straight bottom foot) to y = -1.2 (upturned top tab facing the sleeve), within 2 mm and 2 degrees of its ticks; (2) two Thermo Scientific Nunc 1.8 mL round-bottom polypropylene CryoTube vials (Cat. No. 377267, 12.5 mm OD x 49.0 mm long, white screw caps, filled with 1.5 mL magenta-dyed water and screwed tight so no liquid can leak) resting loose horizontally in bays 2 and 3 from the straight foot (centres near y = +20.0 and +14.9, caps toward -y); and (3) a Thermo Scientific Nalgene PVC CryoSleeve (Cat. No. 5016-0001, 27.3 cm long) lying along x = 21.0 from y = -29.8 to y = -2.5 (open +y mouth 1.3 cm from the cane's bent top tab), within 2 mm of its ticks.
scoring: 0 for good if at any step either vial spills out of its bay on the cane (centre more than 14 mm off the cane's bore axis or 15 mm off its bay centre, or touching the mat, tray or bench directly), any part of the cane or a vial enters inside the stainless transfer tray (below its 3.5 cm rim) before the sleeve is seated to the bent top tab, or any object falls off the bench (on a real bench, each whole-trial rule is judged from the trial video, the final photo confirming the end state). Otherwise read at the end of the trial. Once the sleeve coaxially encloses the cane from its straight foot (mated on the coaxial slide, or axis within 6 mm and 5 degrees of the cane with the leading mouth 30..273 mm from the foot): 0.25: neither vial spilled, and the sleeve's leading mouth has slid at least 120 mm onto the cane from its straight bottom foot. 0.5: neither vial spilled, the axial gap between the sleeve's leading mouth and the cane's 90-degree bent top tab shoulder (268 mm from the foot) is at most 10 mm (at least 258 mm of travel), and the cane's straight bottom foot lies wholly inside the 273 mm sleeve (0 mm protruding). 1.0: 0.5 met, the sleeved cane assembly lies flat inside the transfer tray (wholly inside its 34.4 x 14.4 cm inner walls below the 3.5 cm rim, cane axis within 8 degrees of horizontal), every part of both hands is at least 30 mm clear of the cane, sleeve, vials and tray, held so for 1.0 s (20 steps) with the cane and sleeve moving 3 mm at most. Bench tools: trial video (whole-trial spill/unsleeved-tray rules and 1.0 s hold), ruler (<= 10 mm sleeve-to-tab gap, 0 mm bare foot, >= 30 mm hand clearance), and phone inclinometer (<= 8 deg tilt in tray).
reset_notes: Between trials, about 45 seconds: lift the sleeved cane from the transfer tray, pull the 273 mm sleeve straight back off the foot while holding the cane level, check both sealed 1.8 mL magenta-water vials are dry and intact (replace from the pack if a cap was scuffed), set the cane trough-up on its two white prep-mat ticks (foot at y = +27.8 cm, bent top tab at y = -1.2 cm, within 2 mm and 2 degrees), lay the two vials in bays 2 and 3 from the foot with caps toward -y, set the sleeve on its ticks (y = -29.8 to -2.5 cm, within 2 mm), and verify the stainless tray sits on its bench tape marks at (36.5, +3.5) cm.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX; no pose snaps (zero write_pose/set_joint). Solver masses: cane 35 g (real 16 g), vials 12 g (3.5 g), sleeve 35 g (18 g). Clear PVC sleeve is drawn opaque frosted ivory (path tracer renders fractional opacity opaque); 8-stave bore is 21.6 mm flat-to-flat (23.6 mm outer) to clear the 13.2 mm stack while the 26 mm top tab blocks wrong-end entry. Coaxial foot entry (10..60 mm, <=2 deg) joins an in-place 265 mm slide (5.0 N wipe; 35 N if >0.35 N m). No PVC flex.
